title: PUBG Mobile Arctic Chronicles: Safer Pochinki and Rozhok Landings
summary: Plan safer approaches to Arctic Chronicles hotspots while avoiding predictable Ancient Beast event fights.
intro: The Arctic Chronicles update transforms familiar Erangel areas including Pochinki, Rozhok and Mansion into event locations. A crowded landing can offer quick excitement but little time to collect supplies. Instead of inventing one perfect drop spot, this guide explains how to use flight-path information, line of sight and squad roles to decide whether an Ancient Beast objective is worth contesting.

sections.heading: Read the plane path first
paragraphs: Before marking a hotspot, compare the flight path with the distance to alternate compounds and vehicle spawns you actually recognize. A named event landmark near the flight line will often attract more attention than a distant location, although lobby behavior varies. If the squad wants early combat, choose a safe landing within sight of escape cover. If it wants placement, begin outside the busiest cluster.

sections.heading: Keep the squad close enough to trade
paragraphs: Split landings can work for organized teams, but scattering across several distant rooftops leaves a knocked player impossible to help. Assign two players to the main loot cluster, one to watch a common approach and one to identify a retreat route. Communicate weapon availability rather than guessing who can fight. An unarmed teammate should not sprint toward an Ancient Beast interaction just because the icon appears important.

sections.heading: Approach sealing objectives carefully
paragraphs: The official update describes shooting down sealing towers, activating pedestals and entering the beast after the seal is restored. Each interaction creates a pause during which you may be vulnerable to opponents outside the objective space. Clear nearby angles, listen for movement and have another teammate hold cover before committing. A squad should understand the objective sequence but remain ready to abandon it when the fight turns unfavorable.

sections.heading: Treat special spaces differently
paragraphs: The release describes a shared space inside the beast where combat is disabled. That does not mean the entire route into it is safe. Check the actual boundary before relaxing, and never assume a no-combat rule extends to nearby streets, roofs or exits. If a Hero's Medal enables a special reward, verify its status in the match interface rather than planning around a teammate's unconfirmed memory of the beta.

sections.heading: Rotate away before the zone traps you
paragraphs: A themed attraction can distract a squad from the first safe-zone timer. As soon as the event interaction is finished, check the circle, vehicle availability and nearby gunfire. Use cover between compounds instead of crossing a main road just because an event marker points that way. If enemies hold the obvious exit, a longer route may preserve armor and healing supplies for the next fight.

sections.heading: Practice two landing plans
paragraphs: Prepare a contested plan for when the squad has immediate weapons and a fallback plan for weak opening loot. Run each in several normal matches and review where players were separated or caught reloading. Aim to learn why a route works, not memorize a map from one viral clip. Patch changes and enemy behavior can make an older tactic unreliable, so keep adapting.
